envelope.label: FZP envelope in stories

sources.label: DataSF Zoning Map – Height and Bulk Districts

envelope.method: Stories = min(80, floor(height ft / 10)) (orchestrator rule, tier 3) on the adopted FZP height string of the district with the largest overlap: the Local Program height on Local Program parcels, else the base side. The base height is the current string’s left side, used as the height in force for every roll year (no pre-FZP height map exists, tier 3).

localProgram.label: Local Program eligibility

sources.label: DataSF Zoning Map – Height and Bulk Districts
DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls

localProgram.method: R-4 bulk from h9wh-cg3m; exclusions approximated from wv5m-vpq2; register listings not modelled (assumed eligible, tier 4). Rent control: ≥ 3 non-condo units built before 1979 on the latest roll; hotels: hotel property classes (motels eligible). Lots of 8,000 sf or more get at least 65 ft (§206.10(d)(1)(C)); corner lots are not modelled, so they are understated.

features.label: Redevelopment features (assessor roll)

sources.label: DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls

features.method: Per parcel from the 2025 secured roll (lien date 1 January), roll rows mapped to current parcels through acdm-wktn (retired lots by centroid). Data-quality rules (pipeline/lib/quality-rules/sd.ts, tiers as rule / value, imputed bit in brackets): rows without a roll year (4 / —) or a current parcel (2 / —) are dropped; a year built before 1850 or after the roll year is treated as missing (4 / 2) [bit 0, also set when one of the parcel-year’s rows had its year nulled, even if another row supplies one]; a missing year built or improvement share takes the median of the same land-use class and roll year over observed rows (2 / 2) [bits 0, 2], falling back to the year-wide median, then 0, when the class has none (4 / 4); roll stories above 80 are missing (4 / 2) and missing stories come from the building height (2 / 3) [bit 1]; the units rules of the existing homes (see existingUnits) [bit 3]: units missing on every row of a parcel-year are 0 (4 / 4), units beyond the lot’s capacity are replaced (4 / 2), and a bracketed implausible run is replaced (4 / 2); a roll year missing between two observed years copies the latest earlier year (2 / 2) [bit 5]; a parcel-year without a roll floor area takes the map parcel record’s, rounded to whole m² (2 / 3) [bit 6]. A parcel without a latest-year roll row takes the no-row defaults (4 / 4) [bits 0–4 and 6, imputed 95]: 0 homes, stories from the building height (else 0), land-use class other, the latest year’s "other" medians for year built and improvement share, no rent control, and the map parcel record’s floor area. Assessed values reflect the Prop 13 acquisition basis, not market value. Base-zoning density caps from the Planning Code (tier 1, pipeline/lib/density-caps.ts); a split zoning code takes its most permissive component (sd.zoning.split-code) and generic NCD/NCT codes have no cap (sd.zoning.generic-nc), both tier 4, made up; districts not verified against the official Code default to no cap (NCD, NCT). C-2 and M-1 take the 1 unit per 800 sf floor of their nearest-R-District rule, an approximation that understates (sd.zoning.c2-floor-approx, sd.zoning.m1-floor-approx, tier 4; C-2’s Note 8 no-limit area is not modelled; M-1 allows homes only as a conditional use). RC-4 inside the Van Ness SUD has no density limit, but is capped here because SUD membership isn't in the data (sd.zoning.rc4-vanness-approx, tier 4). SALI has a cap of 0 (residential not permitted); its exceptions, qualifying affordable housing projects and ADUs, are not modelled.

existingUnits.label: Existing homes (assessor)

sources.label: DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls

existingUnits.method: Σ number_of_units over the parcel’s roll rows in the latest roll year (2025); no general LUDB fallback. Units rules (tiers as rule / value, imputed bit 3), in order: a parcel-year whose rows all lack a unit count has 0 (4 / 4); units that would leave under 10 m² of lot area × stories per home take the units of the nearest plausible roll year, else the city land-use (LUDB) count if plausible, else the most homes that fit (4 / 2); a bracketed run of implausible units (≥ 100 and over 10× the neighbouring years) takes the previous year’s value (4 / 2). A roll year missing between two observed years copies the latest earlier year, its bit 3 included (2 / 2, bit 5). A parcel without a latest-year row has 0 (the no-row default, 4 / 4, imputed 95).

yield.label: Units by fill level

sources.label: DataSF Zoning Map – Height and Bulk Districts
DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls

yield.method: Gross units from the project’s typology generator (src/lib/generator, mode max, seed fnv1a32(id)), replacement typologies only, at max(1, round(fill × stories)) for each FILL_LEVELS fill (a tier-4 quantisation grid). FZP yields have no density cap on Local Program parcels and the cap on 2026-10-10 elsewhere; base yields use the base height and the pre-FZP cap (2026-01-11). Ineligible parcels (open space, or no city land-use record and no homes on the roll) have 0: a parcel without a land-use record is eligible when the roll shows homes on it (sd.landuse.none-with-units, 4 / 4), in the panel on each roll year's homes. Base-zoning density caps from the Planning Code (tier 1, pipeline/lib/density-caps.ts); a split zoning code takes its most permissive component (sd.zoning.split-code) and generic NCD/NCT codes have no cap (sd.zoning.generic-nc), both tier 4, made up; districts not verified against the official Code default to no cap (NCD, NCT). C-2 and M-1 take the 1 unit per 800 sf floor of their nearest-R-District rule, an approximation that understates (sd.zoning.c2-floor-approx, sd.zoning.m1-floor-approx, tier 4; C-2’s Note 8 no-limit area is not modelled; M-1 allows homes only as a conditional use). RC-4 inside the Van Ness SUD has no density limit, but is capped here because SUD membership isn't in the data (sd.zoning.rc4-vanness-approx, tier 4). SALI has a cap of 0 (residential not permitted); its exceptions, qualifying affordable housing projects and ADUs, are not modelled.
